News.title: Chilling texts show ‘Temu Barbie’ plot with her mum as she reveals ex’s location before killer drug dealer’s acid attack
News.content:
CHILLING texts show how a woman dubbed “Temu Barbie” and her mum discussed revealing her ex’s location to a drug dealer before he was subject to a fatal acid attack.

The texts lay bare Paris Wilson, 35, agonising over the plot before deciding “at least nobody but Dan gets hurt” as she discussed the plan with her mother Karen.



Winchester Crown Court heard Wilson tipped off drug boss Ryan Kennedy, known as Frost or Frosty, about ex-hubby Danny Cahalane’s movements.

Her ex had been “middle management” in a drug-dealing operation and owed Frost around £120,000 after gambling away drug profits.



On February 21 last year Danny was ambushed by two men who doused him in sulphuric acid at his Plymouth home – Wilson and Danny’s child was in the property at the time.

The dad-of-two suffered catastrophic burns over his entire body and died from his injuries ten weeks later.



Just weeks before the attack, Wilson revealed Frost had offered to reward her if she helped track Danny down.

In one message sent to her mum on January 8, she said: “He said he [Frosty] will pay me a few grand and double what Dan owes you and give you a oz…



“That’s Turkey paid for all of us.”

Moments later she admitted: “But I am worried about my karma.”

She then added: “But at least nobody but Dan gets hurt.”

Wilson went on: “I can’t get her address [a woman Danny was seeing] and tbh that’s the only way I know only Dan would get hurt. Nobody else. And he deserves it. He lies everyday.”

Karen replied: “Then do it your way, but don’t arrange for us to get her from school because that would look like you’d set it up then.”



Wilson answered: “I’ll just be home to get her. He’s always here like 20 past anyways.”

The following day she text her mum: “I’m going to decorate my bedroom this month. And then I need to plan getting to Turkey in Feb before Dan has his limbs cut off.”

Then the next day on January 10 she told her mum Danny had supposedly injured himself putting his arm through glass.



But she added: “I don’t believe he slipped.”

She then texted: “I think someone cut him up.”

Karen replied that she also did not believe the story.

Wilson answered: “Oh yeah no I don’t either lol. I just think he sure does slip over etc a lot. Breaks and loses phones. Like are you okay hun.”

Her mum joked: “That’s because he’s ginger.”



Prosecutors said Wilson had tipped off Frost to Danny’s location on January 19, when members of the gang attempted to kidnap him.

After the failed plot, she texted her mum: “There was black guys here who tried to grab Dan. It genuinely wasn’t me. And he thinks it was.”

Karen replied: “No, don’t be paranoid. They didn’t come near you. It’s not you they want.”



Wilson insisted: “Mum I’d tell you. Because I’d want money. I haven’t told anyone anything.”

The court heard Wilson also expressed concern because Danny and their daughter were together at the property before the fatal acid attack.

Hours after the attack, she texted Karen: “I’ve just calmed down… Mum it was horrific I can’t stop being sick.”

Karen replied: “I’ve just woken up and seen this for f***’s sake.”

The pair then spoke on the phone for around two and a half minutes.



Wilson later texted: “I don’t even know what has happened to Dan, or how bad. But there was still three ambulances when I got there and he was at hospital.”

Wilson was jailed for nine years after being convicted of manslaughter, with a judge saying she was a “key participant” in the plot.

The court heard the relationship between Wilson and Danny had descended into a bitter feud over drugs, money and the daughter they shared.



Following their split, Wilson became a “go-to” contact for the gangster and agreed to reveal Danny’s whereabouts believing Frost would “make her wealthy”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The prosecution said she acted out of greed, revenge, or both.

Two men who carried out the acid attack were convicted of murder, while Wilson was convicted of manslaughter and attempted kidnap before being jailed for nine years.

News.title: Labour’s Bev Craig wins Manchester mayoralty after vote went to second round as she takes over from Andy Burnham
News.content:
RED AGAIN Labour’s Bev Craig wins Manchester mayoralty after vote went to second round as she takes over from Andy Burnham

LABOUR’S Bev Craig will succeed Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester’s new mayor.

Bev received 309,525 votes after the second round, while Reform UK’s Sian Astley received 157,178.



No candidate reached 50 per cent of the vote in the first round, with Bev raking in 251,449 votes and Sian Astley gaining 111,928.

The results represented a huge win for Labour, who swept in 66.3 per cent of the votes.



Reform UK gained 33.7 per cent of the vote.

Reflecting on the victory, Bev said: “The special thank you has to go to the residents of GM.



“To have trust placed in you. I’m honoured, I’m humbled and I stand ready to serve.”

She vowed to “put more money” in the public’s pocket, stressing that everyone deserves a “quality home in a good neighbourhood”.



As the first female metro mayor, Bev promised: “I will defend this city region with every bone in my body and I will fight for a better life for all of us.”

Polling stations closed at 10pm on Thursday, with the count taking place at 9am on Friday.

The turnout was revealed at 2pm today, with 538,659 votes cast from an electorate of 2,142,779, representing the lowest on record for the mayoral role in the region.

The by-election, the largest ever in the UK, used the supplementary vote system, which means people vote for two candidates each.

It comes after Andy Burnham stood down as mayor to become MP for Makerfield, paving the way for him to become Prime Minister earlier this month.

News.title: Trump plans ‘harshest bombing campaign yet’ against Iran to force Tehran’s surrender & ‘Israel will join attacks’
News.content:
DONALD Trump is planning the harshest bombing campaign of the war so far in a bid to finally break Tehran’s resolve, a report says.

US officials claimed the bombardment could begin as early as this weekend and is expected to last several days.



Earlier on Friday, the president told reporters he planned to unleash military strikes on energy infrastructure to force Tehran back to the negotiating table.

Trump predicted that if the US hit Iran hard enough, the hard-line regime would eventually “peter out”.



“We will be hitting them very hard,” Trump said.

“And you know at some point, they’re going to say, ‘We just can’t take it anymore.'”



Israel has been informed of the plans, with the two allies now coordinating what sources say could become one of the harshest bombing campaigns of the conflict.

Iranian state media, quoting a senior official, said any potential US-Israeli attacks would be considered “a form of recklessness”.



Iran has prepared a comprehensive to plan to respond, including strikes on critical infrastructure, it said.

This comes after Trump said earlier this week that “very friendly negotiations” were underway, allowing for a pause in military operations.

Since then, Iran launched a surprise volley of ballistic missiles on troops in Jordan on Tuesday.

In a show of strength, the US swiftly retaliated with a bombardment of its own on the embattled regime.

Announcing the onslaught, US Central Command (Centcom) said they “successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran in response to yesterday’s attempted missile attacks on US forces”.



Washington struck “dozens” of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets, “including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities”.

The strikes aimed to “further diminish threats posed by Iran and its proxies to American forces, commercial shipping, and neighbouring Gulf countries”, Centcom said.

Three people including a child were reportedly killed in attacks on the island of Qeshm – Tehran’s key oil export hub, according to state media.

Explosions were also reported in Khuzestan province to the northwest.

For weeks, Donald Trump has reportedly been telling aides behind closed doors that the Iranians are “crazy”, according to US officials.



He has also complained the interim peace deal was ultimately meaningless, insisting he believed it was always doomed to fail.

Trump’s frustration was plain to see during a meeting at Camp David, where the president branded Iranian diplomats “very dishonourable” to deal with.

He also insisted more devastating military strikes were needed to finally break Tehran’s resolve.

Trump said: “Well, they always want to talk, but they break their words so often.

“All they do is make me angry.”



Iranian diplomats have also expressed exhaustion at the number of times negotiations have broken down with the US.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As the bitter conflict enters its sixth month, neither side appears any closer to giving into demands.

The US continues to insist Iran relinquishes its nuclear program and abandon its control of the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran digging its heels in on both issues.

News.title: Spain’s migrant nightmare is a warning to our PM: get tough or face the same crisis
News.content:
Pain in Spain

THE invasion of Spain by 60,000 illegal migrants may well trigger a Europe-wide emergency.

In just one day, the Spanish government lost all control of its borders as Africans wanting a better economic life poured into the tiny enclave of Ceuta.



Ruthless human trafficking gangs have seized on a ruling by Spain’s Supreme Court that migrants using the sea to reach Ceuta from Morocco cannot be returned.

That decision — coupled with a relaxing of migration laws by Spain’s socialist prime minister — has effectively opened a gateway into Europe.



Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni has suspended freedom of movement arrangements with Madrid.

Other EU leaders are praying ferries linking Ceuta to the mainland will be halted.

If they aren’t, Europe could be about to witness a human wave of illegal migration not matched since more than a million Syrian and other Middle Eastern migrants were waved in.

Inevitably, Britain — with its soft touch approach to asylum, free accommodation and benefits — will be a target in what represents a massive threat to security.

Spain’s nightmare is a warning to our own PM that he must get a grip of the open borders rabble on Labour’s backbenches who are resisting reform.

Unless Andy Burnham gets tough, he may well find himself engulfed in a migrant crisis all of his own.



Rest in BPeace

LABOUR’S Net Zero vandalism is coming home to roost.

BP’s decision to shut down its North Sea operations is proof that the mad dash for decarbonisation is leading to rampant deindustrialisation.

Repeated raids under Labour and the Tories mean the effective tax rate on energy profits is now a completely unsustainable 78 per cent.

Labour’s decision to ban any new drilling in the North Sea was the final nail in the coffin after 60 years of operation.

It’s not just the 1,100 British workers that now face being thrown on the scrapheap.



With no North Sea operations, the fear is BP might even move its headquarters out of Britain altogether.

That would imperil another 14,000 jobs and be a disaster for the economy.

BP’s decision comes as Andy Burnham hints at reversing Ed Miliband’s fanatical opposition to drilling.

The new PM must surely now realise that Net Zero is a monumental act of self-harm.

Go, Gianni

GIANNI Infantino’s empire is crumbling all around him.



His plan to sell off the World Cup lies in tatters and his days in charge of Fifa already look numbered.

Infantino should forget trying to cling on.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His greed has cost him dear.

For football’s sake, he should just go.

News.title: Morocco ‘helped 60,000 migrants overrun Spain border in revenge plot’ before brave locals ‘chased them away with guns’
News.content:
MOROCCO helped facilitate 60,000 migrants overrun a Spanish enclave as diplomatic revenge, Western intelligence sources believe.

People arriving in Ceuta by sea were chased away by locals with guns as the North African city descended into chaos.



Nearly 50,000 are understood to have returned to Morocco in just a day as shops and restaurants keep their shutters down out of fear.

It has since been suggested that Moroccan officials allowed the migrants to storm Ceuta due to tensions with Pedro Sánchez.





They are said to be annoyed by the Spanish prime minister’s pursuit of gas deals with neighbouring Algeria.

Several Moroccans have said they were encouraged to cross the border by authorities.

Youssef Alaoui, 26, told The New York Times that police pointed them in the direction of Ceuta.

He said: “They just kept saying: ‘Go that way, go that way’.”



Mohammed Ahmidho, 37, said he heard about people crossing on social media and that police told him “come to Spain” as he neared the border.

Morocco allowed 8,000 migrants into Ceuta in 2021 following a row with Madrid over its claims to the disputed Western Sahara territory.



At least 60 people have died attempting to reach the enclave over the last 48 hours, either by drowning or being crushed at the border fence.

Terrified locals have had to contend with migrants appearing to break into homes in Ceuta and cars being set alight on the Melilla border.

Europe has since been plunged into crisis, with leaders threatening to suspend free movement with Spain.

Italy has been the first to act – suspending its EU Schengen free-travel deal with the country.



The Schengen agreement is a treaty that allows passport-free travel across 29 European countries.

Finland backed calls for the Mediterranean country to be booted from the pact while France introduced stricter border measures.

Spain’s soft-touch Supreme Court has come under fire and blamed for the recent numbers being so high.

A ruling stated that migrants who arrive by sea should not be subject to immediate expulsion as they are not crossing a physical land border.



The decision has been exploited by people-smuggling gangs and brought with it a wave of undocumented migration.

Sánchez was jeered by locals as he arrived in Ceuta to brand the incident an “attack” and a “violation of the territorial integrity of Spain“.



His socialist government stands out for its pro-migration stance.

It has recently received a huge influx of applications after launching a scheme to provide legal status to 500,000 undocumented migrants.

Moroccan forces beat back crowds with batons and tear gas at the gates to Ceuta on Friday – trying to prevent more from storming across into the tiny Spanish territory.

Water cannon trucks were deployed and the charred remains of a bus and seven cars could be seen from clashes – while Spanish military vehicles lined up on the other side.

Video near the border crossing showed one man wearing Lycra carrying a bike with him in the water alongside hundreds of other migrants rushing to the shore.



Chaos on the beaches of Ceuta, which has a population of under 84,000, spread to the streets as police and local officials struggled to contain the surging numbers.

Some were heard shouting “Long live Spain!” as they dried off in the city.

Shocking reports claim several locals suffered from attempted break-ins at their homes as footage captured multiple alleged incidents.

One shows a man climbing up a ladder as two others hold it still around what appears to be smashed glass from a first floor window.

A second seemingly shows dozens of migrants bundling into a small home and pushing through the tight entrance.



It is unclear if the home was occupied at the time or why so many people were trying to cram inside.

Footage appeared to show dozens of migrants looting a supermarket as cops tried to disperse the crowd and sent the group fleeing down the street.

Enrique Serrano, who runs a women’s clothing store in central Ceuta, said he is being forced to shut up shop due to the fear of violence.

He said: “I’m not opening because the situation is extremely tense. The first thing I have to do is protect my business and my family.”

Another local resident told Spanish TV that shops and other commercial establishments including banks were “shut and locked up”:



They said: “This is like something out of a film. There’s a load of people here from Morocco and Ceuta can’t cope.

“We want to get money out of the bank and we can’t because all the cash machines are blocked.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We had enough to live on for two or three days but we’ve spent what we had and we can’t access any more money. Fights are breaking out in the city. It’s very worrying.

“I’ve bought tickets to leave Ceuta on the 3.30pm ferry to Algeciras to be able to eat and buy food and access cash but I’m still not sure what to do.”

News.title: Eco-guru shot dead on remote farm as cops find ‘goat cult room’ in mysterious cellar & launch £4,250 reward for info
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SHOOTING MYSTERY Eco-guru shot dead on remote farm as cops find ‘goat cult room’ in mysterious cellar & launch £4,250 reward for info

AN ECO-GURU has been shot dead on a remote farm as cops make a shocking discovery in the property’s cellar.

Daniel Emminger, 33, was found dead earlier this year at his home in southwest Germany.



Authorities are now asking for witnesses to come forward, offering a £4,250 reward for any information.

Emminger lived alone on his isolated farm in Bavaria, running a self-sufficient farm.



The victim was violently killed on March 31 in what one detective described as an “execution”.

Bullets have since been recovered from the crime scene, but the weapon has yet to be found.

The leading theory is that the culprit may have disposed of it after carrying out the brutal killing.

While searching the property, investigators found a centuries-old cellar with passages leading deep underground.

Inside officers found a mysterious triangle hanging from the ceiling with a silver goats head attached to it.

Likely used to perform strange rituals, the “goat cult room” has strong links to satanism.



Early findings suggest the murder weapon was fired inside the home.

Given the high calibre of bullet used, the sound would have been more than any human could withstand.

Therefore, the culprit must have worn ear protection or suffered severe hearing damage.

A special investigation team also thinks the perpetrator was experienced in handling firearms.

According to close friends and family, Emminger led an unconventional lifestyle.



He was considered a likeable and charismatic person with a huge group of friends.

However, nvestigators have not ruled out the possibility that disapproval iof his way of life could be the motive for the crime.

Former municipality mayor Jürgen Tempel struck a slightly different note.

“He was what you’d call a dropout,” he told BILD.

“Did he have enemies? He wasn’t an easy person.”



Police believe the perpetrator and the victim knew each other.

Tempel continued: ““He hosted events with up to 150 guests, even though his leased property lacked running water or sewage systems.

“Every fire department has to meet regulations for its festivals. The laws didn’t seem to apply to him.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The 33-year-old was a divorced and had a five-year-old son.

An investigation is ongoing to determine the exact circumstances of his mysterious death.

News.title: Fugitive accused of murder arrested after hiding in Britain as a refugee for 27 years
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KEEPING LOW Fugitive accused of murder arrested after hiding in Britain as a refugee for 27 years

A FUGITIVE accused of murder before fleeing to Britain and posing as a refugee has been arrested after 27 years on the run.

Sabri Sopoti, 60, faces extradition to serve a 24-year jail sentence for shooting a man dead with a machine gun in Albania in 1999.

Prosecutors allege Sopoti got asylum here by pretending to be Kosovo war refugee Zenel Bytyqi.

At Westminster magistrates’ court, he was remanded in custody before a full extradition hearing in December.





Prosecutors say someone rang him in 1999 and told him to “sort out that garbage playing with you and your family”.

His wife later told investigators he became visibly agitated after the call and left home carrying both a machine gun and a pistol.

Sopoti took a Scorpion sub-machine gun and pistol to kill the man in a café.

He vanished and was convicted in his absence.

Albanian authorities allege he fled to Britain using a different identity, claiming to be a refugee from war-torn Kosovo.

They say he was allowed to remain in the UK and lived under the assumed identity for almost three decades before being traced.

His extradition hearing is due to take place in December.

Sopoti was caught in an operation involving Interpol Manchester.

News.title: Jodi Jones’ murderer Luke Mitchell pictured in satanic t-shirt as he cosies up to fiancee in loved-up jail snap
News.content:
JODI JONES’ murderer Luke Mitchell beams for a photo with his fiancee in a creepy jail snap — while wearing a ‘Satanic’ t-shirt.

The 36-year-old lifer – said to be obsessed by the occult – cosied up to Gemma Chapman as the couple had their portrait taken during a prison visit.



Monster Mitchell – who refuses to admit stabbing and mutilating Jodi, 14 in 2003 – has a red-horned demon emblazoned across his chest in the sick pic.

Mitchell also had a collection of devil-themed books on his Christmas wish list — including The Satanic Bible.



His hand-written note from behind bars also features other macabre tomes by Church of Satan founder Anton LaVey.

We can reveal Jodi Jones’ killer requested copies of The Devil’s Notebook, The Satanic Witch, Satan Speaks and The Satanic Rituals by the late US oddball, whose devotees would strip naked on his altar and preach sexual freedom.

Mitchell, 36, was said to have been obsessed with the occult in June 2003 when he repeatedly stabbed 14-year-old girlfriend Jodi and slit her throat in woods near her home in Dalkeith, Midlothian.

Leaked notebooks suggested he was a dope-smoking devil worshipper infatuated with goth rocker Marilyn Manson and the unsolved murder of actress Elizabeth Short — whose naked body was found cut in half in the infamous 1947 Black Dahlia case.



The latest revelations came as pictures emerged showing Mitchell in a devil t-shirt while posing in jail with fiancée Gemma Chapman.

We told how the fiend, who continues to insist he is the victim of a miscarriage of justice, was denied his freedom in April 2024 after psychiatric reports established he remained a “sexual risk” to women.

A source said: “Luke Mitchell has spent the last 20-odd years insisting he is innocent but he’s spent just as much time obsessing about Satan.

“It’s an odd choice of t-shirt if he’s trying to convince folk he doesn’t have a dark side.”

“He wants the world to think he is a clean-living angel who doesn’t pose a threat to anyone.



“So he’ll be furious when the public get to see the darker side of his character. There’s good reason he wasn’t granted parole two years ago because he hasn’t changed a bit.”

We can reveal Mitchell also asked for goods from arts and crafts retailer Dryad Education for Christmas — adding “left handed” to the scrawled note which also gave his shoe size as ten.



Balding and bearded Mitchell was seen in public for the first time in 15 years on Thursday as he was briefly allowed out of jail amid tight security for his mum’s funeral.

He emerged cuffed to a guard at the send-off for Corinne following her death at 66 after a health battle.

Long-term partner Gemma — whom he reportedly proposed to at high-security Shotts nick in November 2024 — was by his side at Mortonhall Crematorium in Edinburgh.

In a picture of the couple understood to have been taken at the Lanarkshire jail this year, Mitchell is seen wearing a five-starred pentacle pendant — a symbol of paganism — and a Superman T-shirt.



In another image taken previously Mitchell beams in a t-shirt emblazoned with a devil image while leaning lovingly on Gemma’s shoulder. The lifer also wore a pair of flashy red and black Balmain Unicorn low-top sneakers which cost up to £1,000 new.

Mitchell was previously last seen in public with braids in his hair 15 years ago during a doomed bid to overturn his conviction at the Court of Criminal Appeal in Edinburgh.

His frenzied murder of Jodi shocked the country. As well as a slashed throat, she had also suffered sickening wounds to her ear, mouth, breast and abdomen.

Mitchell claimed his dog led him to Jodi’s naked and mutilated body during a search.

He insisted he was innocent but in January 2005 a jury found the then 16-year-old guilty following a 42-day trial at the High Court in Edinburgh.



Lord Nimmo jailed him for at least 20 years for the “truly evil murder”.

No DNA link to the crime was ever established — leading campaigners to argue Mitchell, of Newbattle, Midlothian was wrongly convicted.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 2012 he took a lie detector test in a bid to prove his innocence.

In February last year he lost a legal challenge over the Parole Board for Scotland’s decision to keep him locked up.

News.title: Manchester mayoral election results LIVE: Labour's Bev Craig WINS over Reform and takes over from Andy Burnham
News.content:
Results for Britain's biggest-ever by-election are expected at any moment, with Labour confident Bev Craig will be named Mayor of Greater Manchester at some point this evening

The Mayor of Greater Manchester race will progress to a second round of votes, it has been confirmed, as Labour's Bev Craig hopes to succeed Andy Burnham.

Following a long night of counting across Greater Manchester, Craig and Reform UK's Sian Astley will be going through to the second round. Tom Stannard, Manchester returning officer, told counters at Manchester's Co-op Live arena that a second preference count will take place.

He has told counters to "focus on accuracy over speed" after several hours of waiting in the room. Ms Craig is the favourite to succeed Andy Burnham, who vacated the post when he became MP for Makerfield last month. The new Prime Minister has since set up a No10 in the North in the heart of Manchester.

Reform UK were initially tipped to be a strong challenger for the coveted post, which is set to become more powerful as Mr Burnham devolves power from Westminster.

News.title: Bev Craig succeeds Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester Mayor in major Labour victory
News.content:
Bev Craig succeeds Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester Mayor in major Labour victory

The Greater Manchester mayor vote was triggered after Andy Burnham’s resignation from the role last month following his Makerfield parliamentary election victory, which paved the way for his No10 bid

View 5 Images Bev Craig is the new Mayor of Greater Manchester (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Wire)

Bev Craig has been crowned Andy Burnham’s successor as mayor of Greater Manchester today after a comfortable victory in the country’s biggest ever by-election.

The 41-year-old leader of Manchester City Council and rising star in the Labour Party won in a run-off with Reform's Sian Astley after no candidate won more than 50% of the vote.

Turnout in the race was just over 25% - down on the last mayoral contest in the region - with more than 500,000 ballots cast out of an eligible two million voters taking part. After the run-off vote, taking into account voters' second preferences, Ms Craig achieved 309,525 of the votes.

‌



View 5 Images Ms Craig comfortably beat Reform UK runner-up Sian Astley (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Wire)

The vote was triggered after Mr Burnham’s resignation from the role last month following his Makerfield parliamentary election victory, which paved the way for his Downing Street bid.

The victory for Ms Craig, who is friends with the new Prime Minister, came despite Reform’s early hopes of a major political upset in Labour’s heartland after the party’s success in the region at the May local elections.

But with Nigel Farage distracted by his own fight with Count Binface in a by-election in Clacton and evidence of a ‘Burnham bounce’ in the national polls, surveys suggested in recent days Ms Craig was on course for a comfortable win in Greater Manchester.

View 5 Images Labour Party supporters react to the results (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Wire)

Labour overtakes Reform in two major polls while Nigel Farage argues with a bin READ MORE :

Ms Craig, who grew up on a council estate just outside Belfast, moved to Manchester in 2003 at the age of 18 as a student and was first elected as a Burnage councillor in 2011.

‌



She became the first LGBT+ and first female leader of Manchester City Council 10 years later - taking over from Sir Richard Leese, who had held the position for a quarter of a century.

View 5 Images Labour's Bev Craig on the campaign trail with new PM Andy Burnham (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

In a recent interview with The Mirror, Ms Craig said her friendship and good working relationship with the new Prime Minister - who once "DJ’ed badly" at her birthday - will help Greater Manchester.

‌



But she added: “Do not underestimate my ability to hold anyone’s feet to the fire when it means getting what we need for Greater Manchester.

View 5 Images Labour's canddiate in the Greater Manchester Mayoral contest, Bev Craig (Image: Annabelle Lee-Ellis/PA Wire)

“When people ask what’s the difference between you and Andy - there’s loads of differences. But I am standing as my own person, with my own ideas, and I’ll be accountable to this region, and to no one else.”

‌



Mr Burnham was among those seen on Thursday evening casting his ballot at a polling station in Golborne, near Wigan, less than an hour before polls closed.

News.title: Paedophile grandad avoids jail after police find sickening images of children
News.content:
Paedophile grandad avoids jail after police find sickening images of children

James Barber, 52, was caught with indecent images of children as young as six and had discussed rape fantasy and paedophilia in messages recovered from his phone

View 2 Images James Barber leaving court (Image: Liverpool Echo)

A grandfather has avoided jail despite police finding dozens of sickening images of children on his phone.

James Barber, 52, was also caught discussing rape fantasy and paedophilia in messages recovered from the device.

He appeared in court today and pleaded guilty to three counts of making indecent images of children and possession of extreme pornographic images.

Barber, of Kitchener Street in St Helens, was arrested in June last year after a search warrant was issued at his home.

There, police recovered several Category A images - the most severe form of indecent images of children - with some involving children as young as six.

View 2 Images Barber denied he was sexually attracted to children (Image: Liverpool Echo)

The court heard the defendant possessed 16 category A images, 18 category B images, 11 category C images and three extreme pornographic images, reports the Liverpool Echo.

When he was interviewed by police, Barber denied he was sexually attracted to children and said he had seen indecent images on messaging platform Kik.

But officers also recovered message chats from the defendant's phone in which he spoke of rape fantasy and paedophilia.

Prosecutor Iain Criddle argued Barber had the images on his phone because of a sexual attraction to children.

Andrew McInnes, defending, said Barber accepted the seriousness of the offences and displayed "evidence of guilt and shame"

The defence also noted Barber's "long term" use of cocaine, and alcohol as a contributing factor in his "risk taking behaviour online", adding that he had "disappeared down a very dark hole".

The defence said Barber had since stopped using cocaine, reduced his alcohol consumption "considerably" and would "welcome any assistance to remain drug free".

Mr McInnes added: "The defendant is now a grandad. While he now has the support of his family, there is no doubt, going forward, that there will be strains upon family relationships because of these offences.

"While they support him, they do not condone this behaviour in any way," he added.

Judge Ian Harris said that while he recognised Barber had "addressed" his cocaine habit, there were concerns about his potential to reoffend.

"This type of offending is vile," Judge Harris said. "There is no other word for it. It is repellent to right thinking members of our community and society generally.

"The author of the pre-sentence report sets out that you demonstrated a comprehensive understanding of the harms that your behaviour can cause, although it seems that did not occupy your mind at the time you were using that type of paedophile material.

"If it was not for people like you, there would not be a market for this type of material and the consequent abuse to children that is caused by people who create the images of child abuse in order for it to be distributed. You, bluntly, perpetuate that market."

Barber was sentenced to a three-year community order with a nine-month drug rehabilitation requirement and a rehabilitation activity requirement of up to 25 days, as well as 120 hours of unpaid work.

He was also made subject to a five year Sexual Harm Prevention Order and a five year notification requirement, requiring him to notify police of specified personal details under the Sex Offenders Register.

‌



Barber has one previous conviction from 2021 for drink driving and a caution for assault in 2006. Neither were deemed as aggravating factors in the sentencing.

The defendant was also ordered to pay £250 in court costs.

Judge Harris told the court that Barber would not be given a prison sentence in order to allow him to "engage in appropriate and necessary opportunities" to address his behaviour.

‌



But the judge said a breach of orders could result in immediate imprisonment.

"In plain English the interests of the community at large, in my judgement, are better served by you receiving a rehabilitative order to avoid this type of offending in the future," Judge Harris said.

"If you fail to cooperate with the authorities that will assist you then you will be breached, a summons will be issued. I reserve all breaches to the crown court in the hope that there will not be any.

Article continues below

"You must know that there are real teeth to these orders and they can bite very hard."

News.title: 'Jealous' man who assassinated ex's new lover with samurai sword gets life
News.content:
'Jealous' man who assassinated ex's new lover with samurai sword gets life

Michael Bretton, 41, of Shaftesbury, Dorset, was convicted of stabbing Craig Hurcombe, 39, with a samurai sword before burying him in a shallow grave

View 5 Images Michael Bretton has been convicted of murder (Image: Avon & Somerset Police/PA Wire)

A man who murdered his former lover’s new partner by stabbing him with a samurai sword has been jailed for life, with a minimum term of 29 years and six months.

‌



Michael Bretton, 41, of Shaftesbury, Dorset, was convicted by a unanimous jury of killing Craig Hurcombe, 39, in Gurney Slade, Somerset, on January 1. Bristol Crown Court heard Bretton ambushed Mr Hurcombe at his work before stabbing him – leaving a fatal injury likened to the type seen in a “historical battle”.

‌



After the murder, Bretton attempted to burn Mr Hurcombe’s clothes and body before burying him in a shallow grave in nearby woodland. Judge William Hart sentenced Bretton, who worked in a chocolate factory, to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 29 years and six months.

‌



View 5 Images Craig Hurcombe was killed with a sword (Image: Avon & Somerset Police/PA Wire)

The judge said Bretton’s claims during his trial that Mr Hurcombe, a lorry driver from Devizes, Wiltshire, had died in an accident were “wholly fabricated”.

"It was an account which, both in its content and in the way you told it, convinced me that you are a very dangerous man with an obsessive personality,” he told Bretton.

‌



“You are entirely self-centred and portrayed a person who was sorry for yourself in a way that was obscene.”

Judge Hart said he was “entirely satisfied” that it was correct to describe the murder as an assassination. During the trial, jurors were told how Mr Hurcombe had been in a relationship with a woman called Kate Saunders for years until they separated in 2023.

Two years later, Ms Saunders and Bretton met through an online dating website and had a casual relationship. She then rekindled her relationship with Mr Hurcombe, with Bretton “motivated by jealousy”, the judge said.

‌



View 5 Images Screengrab taken from bodyworn video showing the arrest of Michael Bretton (Image: Avon & Somerset Police/PA Wire)

Bretton began to stalk and track Mr Hurcombe’s movements, fitting a tracker to the couple’s cars. On January 1, Bretton used the “cover of darkness” and dark clothing to hide at Mr Hurcombe’s work, Blanchard’s yard.

“You took with you a most fearsome weapon, a samurai sword,” the judge said. “You went there intending to murder him and you did exactly that. You took him by surprise. You slew him. He tried to fend off the sword but it was hopeless and in vain."

‌



“You thrust the blade through almost the full thickness of his body, the most extraordinary injury. The sort of injury more associated with historical battle than modern-day life.”

Bretton then dragged Mr Hurcombe’s body away, stripped him of his clothes and buried his body in a shallow grave. He took Mr Hurcombe’s Sim card from his phone, using it to communicate with his concerned family and friends for the next 10 days.

The judge described the evidence against Bretton as “compelling” but highlighted one mistake he made as sealing his fate. “I hope it haunts you,” the judge told him. “I very much doubt you are haunted by what you did to Craig.”

‌



View 5 Images Craig Hurcombe's burnt out car (Image: Avon & Somerset Police/PA Wire)

This mistake was Bretton driving his mother’s car – complete with a tracking system that recorded journeys travelled – to a bridge where he disposed of the sword. Police later downloaded the journeys from the vehicle and discovered he had stopped for three minutes by the River Stour near the town of Sturminster Newton.

Divers attended the scene and recovered the sword, which a pathologist later confirmed could have inflicted the fatal wound on Mr Hurcombe. Mr Hurcombe was reported missing by his mother, Nicola Hurcombe, on January 10. His body was discovered on January 14.

‌



Pathologist Dr Amanda Jeffery, who carried out a post-mortem examination on Mr Hurcombe’s body, concluded he had died from a single stab injury which penetrated through his torso.

In a victim impact statement, Mrs Hurcombe described how her son was hard-working and much loved by his family and friends.

“The fact my son has been murdered feels like the end of the world to me,” she said. “Craig didn’t deserve this in anyway whatsoever. He was a wonderful, kind and decent person and had been that way all his life.”

‌



View 5 Images Screengrab taken from CCTV showing Craig Hurcombe waving to the camera (Image: Avon & Somerset Police/PA Wire)

In a direct address to Bretton, she described him as “a vile, deluded, despicable individual who is nothing more than a heartless, cold-blooded murderer”. Ms Saunders told the court her devastation at Mr Hurcombe’s death was “visceral”.

“Michael Bretton, I will never forgive you for what you have done,” she told Bretton. “No punishment that you will receive will ever compare to the pain you have inflicted on me.”

Article continues below

Representing Bretton, Andrew Langdon KC said his client had served in the Royal Navy for five years and had been supported during his trial by his mother and sister. Speaking after the case, Detective Inspector Neil Meade, of Avon and Somerset Police, said: “Bretton is one of the most dangerous individuals I have ever dealt with.

“His behaviour, including the stalking of Kate and the extraordinary lengths he went to in order to control and influence both Craig and Kate’s lives, was deeply disturbing.

“The level of planning and premeditation behind Craig’s murder was horrific. Throughout the investigation, Bretton appeared almost arrogant in the extensive measures he took to cover his tracks and evade responsibility.”

News.title: Remains of missing boy, 14, pulled from River Taw after weeks of searching
News.content:
Remains of missing boy, 14, pulled from River Taw after weeks of searching

Taylor Charlton was 14 when he disappeared from Barnstaple in Devon on May 8, sparking a massive search and rescue effort from the local community and emergency services

View Image Taylor Charlton was 14 when he went missing in February (Image: Karl Grafton <karlgrafton@hotmail.com>)

Police have confirmed that human remains found in a river in Devon are missing teenager Taylor Charlton.

Taylor, 14 at the time of his disappearance, went missing on the night of Friday May 8 in Barnstaple, sparking an extensive operation to find him.

Police said the support shown by the local community since Taylor was reported missing had been "tremendous".

Volunteers and members of the police searched tirelessly to find Taylor. Tragically, Devon and Cornwall Police confirmed today that remains found in the River Taw on June 24 belonged to Taylor, Devon Live reports.

Police arrested a 20-year-old man on suspicion of murder on June 12. He was later released on bail while investigations continued.

On July 2, a woman in her 40s was also arrested on suspicion of murder. She has since been released on bail pending further enquiries.

Police say there is an ongoing investigation into the circumstances of Taylor's death, and detectives will "continue to establish the full facts".

Devon and Cornwall Police said: “Taylor’s family have been updated of this development and our thoughts and condolences are with them, Taylor’s friends and the local community.

“Taylor’s loved-ones continue to be supported by specialist officers at this incredibly difficult and distressing time.

“We respectfully ask that the family’s privacy is respected as they come to terms with this tragic news.

“This is not the outcome that anyone hoped for and we know how deeply this will affect the local community who have shown tremendous support throughout the search.

“An investigation into the circumstances surrounding Taylor’s death remains ongoing and detectives will continue to establish the full facts.”

Article continues below

Police have asked people not to speculate about the case or share unconfirmed information online while enquiries continue.

Anyone with information that could help the investigation has been asked to contact police.

News.title: Faces of victims betrayed by 'monster' funeral director Robert Bush as families fume at 'atrocious' sentence
News.content:
Faces of victims betrayed by 'monster' funeral director Robert Bush as families fume at 'atrocious' sentence

Families of dozens of Robert Bush's victims have condemned the sentence he received after bodies were left to rot and the wrong ashes handed out at his Legacy funeral parlour

View 9 Images Dozens of people were victimised by Bush after their deaths (Image: Humberside Police/PA Wire)

These are the faces of the victims betrayed by "monster" Legacy funeral director Robert Bush, whose families have been left furious after he was handed a "joke" 20 year sentence for crimes.

‌



Bush, 48, the owner of Legacy Independent Funeral Services in Hull, East Yorkshire, left bodies to rot - including the remains of a miscarried baby - in his mortuary, and gave the wrong ashes to bereaving families, while conning other clients to fund a life of luxury. He pleaded guilty to 67 offences spanning 12 years, including 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial - which affected hundreds of families - and was today sentenced to 20 years behind bars after he abused their trust "on an industrial scale".

‌



Furious family members condemned the sentence as "atrocious" and a "joke" after 35 bodies and half a tonne of ashes were recovered from the home - with more victims feared.

‌



'Monster' funeral director Robert Bush jailed for 20 years as heartbroken families demand public inquiry READ MORE :

View 9 Images Bush victimised 300 people (Image: Humberside Police/PA Wire)

Hull Crown Court heard that Bush had defrauded nearly 200 families out of £500,000, and acted out of "financial greed" while mishandling victims' remains and handing out the wrong ashes to their loved ones. Sentencing today, Judge Mr Justice Hilliard said he had "caused anguish and pain on a scale beyond comprehension".

View 9 Images Bush was sentenced to 20 years behind bars today (Image: Elizabeth Cook/PA Wire)

‌



He said in his remarks that, unless a body was among those recovered and identified by police following a raid on Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull in 2024, people who used the service can't be "absolutely certain they received the ashes of their loved one".

Police have been able to identify the remains recovered during that raid, with their family members - up to 300 people - among Bush's many victims.

The court was told relatives of 46 people who were cremated between 2017 and 2024 were given the wrong ashes and the loved ones of another 11 deceased never received any. The court also heard from some of the 226 pensioners who said they had been “conned” out of what little savings they had after being sold fake funeral plans by Bush.

‌



He pleaded guilty to 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial and 30 counts of fraud by false representation relating to bodies found at the site, four “foetus allegations” of fraud, where he presented ashes to women falsely saying that they were “the remains of their unborn”, a further charge of fraud covering the ashes of 57 people between 2017 and 2024, fraudulent trading relating to funeral plans between 2012 and 2024 and theft from 12 charities.

The judge said following Bush's sentencing today that he had “never known offences affect so many people so deeply”, adding that the ex-mortician "must have a heartless side to him - which allowed him to treat the living and the dead in the way he did, and he was very confident he would get away with what he was doing".

View 9 Images Stephen Perrins was also identified as a victim of Bush's (Image: PA)

‌



The judge said: "How betrayed they now feel." Families remained silent and hugged as he was jailed while Bush simply stood up with his hands clasped in front while leaving the dock.

They hugged and wept after leaving the court, and told the Mirror of their anguish as they reacted to the sentence Bush received. One woman said: "He should never come out again for what he’s done." Another added: “He’s only going to be 58 when he comes out. It’s a joke.”

Tristan Essex, 26, said: “We’ve been failed again! We’ve waited two and a half years for this!” Michaela Baldwin, whose stepfather Danny Middleton’s body was found at Legacy, said the sheer number of people victimised by him should have warranted at least another decade behind bars for Bush.

‌



View 9 Images One of Danny Middleton's family members said Bush should have gotten 30 years behind bars (Image: PA)

She said: “I understand that no matter what the judge would have given him, it wouldn’t be long enough for us, but still 20 years is still… If you think there’s bodies that was involved in this, and that’s less than a year for each."

“[He should have got] at least 30 – one year for each, at least. I hate him, I’ll always hate him, there’s just so much greed in why he’s done this.” Joanne Moody, whose father Peter Moody was one of the bodies found at Legacy, said Robert Bush’s sentence was “atrocious”.

‌



She said: “It’s a joke, he’s going to be out in 10 years. There’s no justice for any of us, we’re all still going to be kicking around when he gets out. We’re not going to get closure.”

View 9 Images The Legacy case has moved the Government into action on regulating funeral providers (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

Phil and Jackie Groizard believe they were given the wrong ashes for Mr Groizard’s mother-in-law Carol, and said Bush appeared to have simply scooped some random remains into a bag for them when they inquired. Mrs Groizard said Bush’s sentence was “not long enough.” She said: “He’ll only be 58 when he comes out. He’s got away with it – it should have been life."

Article continues below

The Government pledged to formally regulate the funeral sector following Bush's sentencing, with the Department for Health and Social Care issuing a statement announcing the move. A spokesperson said regulation would be a priority “following the harrowing case in Hull”.

Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper said: “In the wake of this horrific case, we will now bring forward comprehensive proposals to ensure respect and dignity for the deceased in every setting, including proper regulation of the funeral sector.”

News.title: Fire and 'explosions' at Washington factory as 'close windows' warning issued
News.content:
Thick black smoke coming from the scene of the fire

Emergency services rushed to the incident at a factory in the Crowther Industrial Estate, Washington, in Tyne and Wear, with witnesses telling of 'several explosions'

Massive plumes of smoke can be seen coming from a raging fire at a factory after reports of "several explosions" in the North East.

Emergency services rushed to the incident in the Crowther Industrial Estate, Washington, in Tyne and Wear, with witnesses saying that there's no signs of the fire easing.

Northumbria Police says officers are on the scene to support the Tyne and Wear Fire and Rescue Service in responding to the fire in Washington, with a 'cordon currently in place'.

Pictures from the scene show five fire brigade appliances and an aerial ladder platform dispatched. Thick black smoke is billowing into the sky which can be seen for miles.

News.title: Watch: Moroccan police clash with migrants near border with Spain's Ceuta
News.content:
Tens of thousands of migrants have entered Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, with many swimming and using inflatables to travel from Morocco.

Others ran through a gate in the border fence.

The territory's leader, Juan JesÃºs Vivas, said the number of arrivals has been overwhelming resources and urged the Spanish government to intervene.

Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez described the situation as an "attack" and said all illegal migrants would be returned to Morocco "as soon as possible".

Ceuta, on Morocco's northern coast, has long been a focal point for migrants attempting to reach Europe.

More than 25,000 have returned to Morocco voluntarily so far, officials said.

More on this story.

News.title: Fifa executive says staff 'deceived' by Infantino plans
News.content:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino's position came under further scrutiny on Friday as the governing body's chief operating officer strongly criticised his plan to sell stakes in competitions to private investors.

In a statement released to the Associated Press, Kevin Lamour described the controversial plans as "the project of one person" and said "the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions".

He added Fifa's own administration was "deceived" about the project. BBC Sport has approached Fifa for comment.

The lengthy statement did not mention Infantino by name.

It came on the same day a third confederation spoke out against the plans, a senior adviser to Infantino resigned, and Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the Swiss was "the wrong man" to lead Fifa.

US President Donald Trump - addressing the proposals for the first time - said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans.

The two have developed a close relationship since Trump assumed office for a second time in 2025.

Lamour said in his statement: "Our mission - the mission of the hundreds of passionate, dedicated, and exemplary Fifa employees - is to serve football.

"A president must bring people together, unite them, and inspire them. Today, we are experiencing the opposite."

Lamour acknowledged he had a duty of loyalty to his employer but also to "certain values" and supporting his colleagues.

"If that means I lose my job, then so be it," he added. "I will understand and respect that decision. At least I'll sleep well tonight."

News.title: No sentence long enough for jailed funeral director Robert Bush, say families
News.content:
Karen Dry, who organised monthly vigils for the victims' families when the investigation began, said: "No sentence was ever going to be enough."

She said families were hoping Bush would be sentenced to more than 30 years, but what was "really messing with people's heads" was the prospect of him only serving half of his sentence.

When asked does it feel fair? She replied: "No, it really doesn't.

"For some people, I totally get that today is the end of it for them.

"But I'm my mam and dad's daughter, and we are a bit more determined than just letting these things lie."

She said without regulation of the industry, "in five or 10 years' time there will be another funeral director with another 300 families in a courtroom somewhere".

"We've got to put a stop to it and it's got to stop now."

News.title: Israeli official says troops won't pull back in Gaza without 'genuine' Hamas disarmament
News.content:
A senior Israeli official has said troops will not pull back from their current positions in Gaza without the "genuine disarmament" of Palestinian armed group Hamas in the territory.

Hamas meanwhile said handing over its heavy weapons was contingent on Israel ending "all forms of aggression" and withdrawing its forces from Gaza.

It comes after Donald Trump said the Board of Peace had reached an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

On Friday Trump insisted that Israel was "very happy" with the proposed agreement, describing it as a "big step for the Middle East". However far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir dismissed the draft as "not acceptable".

It is part of the second phase of a US-brokered Gaza ceasefire plan that aims to end the war in Gaza.

The 20-point plan, unveiled in September last year, included the creation of the Board of Peace to oversee the agreement's implementation, as well as the disarmament of Hamas, withdrawal of Israeli troops and reconstruction of Gaza.

Speaking at a cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, Trump said he had an "understanding" with Israel over the latest disarmament proposal agreed with Hamas, adding that "Israel's very happy about it".

Asked whether Hamas would disarm before Israeli forces withdrew from Gaza or vice versa, Trump did not answer directly but said Gaza remained "a very complex situation".

Hamas weapons would be handed over to the Board of Peace, he added.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has not yet commented on the latest proposal.

News.title: How Sam Fender and Olivia Dean's Rein Me In broke the UK's singles chart record
News.content:
This reworking of Rein Me In, from Fender's third studio album, the Mercury Prize-winning People Watching, features an extra verse about the breakdown of a relationship from a female perspective, from Dean.

"[It's] very personal and reminded us of home, but when Olivia put her touch on it, it became a much more universal track," he told Radio 1, adding "that's what made it so huge and so beautiful".

He said he wanted to "personally thank" Dean, who helped him achieve his first ever number one single, adding: "It wouldn't have happened without Olivia obviously, but now I feel like it belongs to the fans, they've made it what it is".

When asked how he'd be celebrating the achievement, Fender joked "I think I'm just gonna have a really big sandwich".

It hasn't been a straightforward ascent to the top for Rein Me In - originally released as a solo Fender track and repurposed as a duet in June 2025, it took eight months to reach number one in February this year.

Dean said when the track came out, external that the original version of Rein Me In was her "favourite song on Sam's album" and it was "a pleasure to write a new verse from a female perspective".

A lot of the song's success as a duet comes from its authenticity, with the lyrics exploring the fallout from the end of a relationship and the difficulties faced by both parties as they try to move on from each other.

Whilst Fender's verses feel full of anger and regret at not being able to open up and be the partner he wanted to be, they are complimented by the softer and more reflective tone of Dean's, in which she encourages him to try again to make it work.

It has been described by Blunt Magazine's Jake Fitzpatrick, external as "stormy, tender and anthemic" and a "love letter to the kind of songwriting that knows when to burn slow".

The song has also received praise amongst many critics and bloggers, including Cult Following's Ewan Gleadow, external, who says that Dean's addition helps it to find "a new depth", noting "charm is a big part of it too, with all those reflections on where you come from and where you're headed".

News.title: Snapchat joins other popular platforms in fight against 'AI slop'
News.content:
As Chris Best, the co-founder and chief executive of Substack put it last week: "It's getting harder to tell what's real on the internet."

Announcing a new tool, external designed to let readers on the newsletter platform detect AI-generated writing, Best cited other research that has found up to 40% of writing on social media is now fake or AI-generated.

"Platforms that reward fakeness will create a race to the bottom," Best said.

LinkedIn, a social media platform focused on work, introduced a button on its platform this week that allows any user to report if a post or a comment appears to be AI-generated.

"AI slop is a top priority for all of us," LinkedIn's chief product officer Hari Srinivasan wrote on the platform.

In just the last couple of months, he said the platform had "blocked billions" of attempts to post AI-generated comments.

"Every day we are now catching hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts," Srinivasan said.

Like Snap, LinkedIn said it is not rejecting the use of AI entirely and users that use AI tools to "refine" their posts should not get caught up in efforts to combat AI slop.

Nonetheless, LinkedIn is removing an automated prompt that would show up for users writing a post offering to "enhance" it through the use of AI. It will go back to a simple proofreading tool.

YouTube, the video platform owned by Google, also this month updated its policies, external around what kind of content can be monetised by creators.

Research from last year found scores of channels on YouTube that were solely AI-generated content, external, many of which had millions of subscribers and some of which made millions of dollars in revenue.

In an effort to discourage YouTube from filling up with what the platform calls "inauthentic content", earlier this month the site broke down into three categories the kind of videos that will not be allowed to make money through it: generic, repetitive, or template-based.

Those styles of content are much easier to make, and quickly, with the use of generative AI tools.

YouTube's trust and safety chief Matt Halprin said in an interview, external on the updated rules that, while AI tools can help people with their content, they are more frequently being used to create fake and low-quality videos.

"The same technology really enables great stuff," Halprin said.

"But it also enables stuff that's kind of content farming, and that's the stuff that we don't want to have."

News.title: Two more small boat pilots jailed for Channel crossings
News.content:
Two men who piloted overcrowded small boats have been jailed for endangering others while crossing the Channel.

Omar Heidari, a 34-year-old Afghan national who steered a dinghy carrying 95 people to the UK in June, has been jailed for two years.

Manas Yuk, an 18-year-old Sudanese national, was sentenced to 18 months in youth detention after piloting a boat carrying 81 people - including a number of children - just days prior.

The men were sentenced at Canterbury Crown Court on Friday having earlier pleaded guilty to endangerment.

It means 10 people have now been sentenced under a law targeting those who risk the safety of others by piloting small boats since it came into force in January.

The Home Office said Heidari had endangered the largest number of lives of anyone so far sentenced for the offence.

The boat was overcrowded during the crossing on 23 June, with some passengers hanging their legs over the sides of the vessel, it said. A number of the passengers were not wearing life jackets.

He was jailed for endangering others as well as arriving in the UK without valid entry clearance.

News.title: Parents sue school over 'inhumane' calming rooms after BBC report
News.content:
Parents are suing a special school after a BBC investigation uncovered CCTV footage showing autistic children being locked inside calming rooms and abused.

Ten families are claiming that their children â all of whom had learning disabilities or several mental disorders - were amongst those harmed by their treatment in the rooms.

A police investigation into the abuse, recorded inside the rooms at Whitefield special school in north London, ended two years ago without any charges.

The school is now run by a new trust which says the failings have led to "important learning".

Many special schools use seclusion spaces such as calming rooms outside of classrooms to address sensory needs or challenging behaviour.

But the leaked footage obtained by the BBC showed children being shoved into padded rooms, thrown to the floor, restrained by the neck - or left alone, sitting in vomit.

One 12-year-old boy appeared in over 55 hours of CCTV footage filmed inside the rooms.

At the time, the Children's Commissioner for England, Dame Rachel de Souza, said the use of the rooms was "horrifying".

Leigh Day is now bringing a civil legal claim on behalf of 10 families against the trust which ran the school and the London borough of Waltham Forest.

The law firm says the use of the rooms was "barbaric", according to its clients. The claim alleges that children were falsely imprisoned and their human rights were breached.

"What was done to these children was profoundly harmful, and its impact continues to be felt by families every day", says Alison Millar, who is leading the case.

The CCTV obtained by the BBC had been recorded between 2014 and 2017 but only emerged in 2021.

Last month, a long-delayed review commissioned by Waltham Forest found that restraint and seclusion became "normalised" and a culture developed that allowed "pejorative views of non-compliant children".

It added that parents were clear that the practices were "unimaginable" and "inhumane".

The BBC has also found evidence of mistreatment in seclusion rooms at other schools across the UK.

CCTV from a different school showed a boy being "brutally" and "unlawfully" restrained, while elsewhere an autistic child was kept inside a cage.

Hilliard warned that unless a body was one of those recovered by police in 2024 and properly identified, no-one who had used Legacy's cremations services "at any time can be absolutely certain they received the ashes of their loved one".

"He must have a heartless side to him - which allowed him to treat the living and the dead in the way he did, and he was very confident he would get away with what he was doing."

The judge added: "I don't think I have ever known offences affecting so many people and so deeply."

The court was told relatives of 46 people who were cremated between 2017 and 2024 were given the wrong ashes and the loved ones of another 11 never received any.

"Husbands and wives, partners, parents, children, grandchildren, now discovering that they are left with nothing, or in some cases we heard, an empty plastic bag or a teaspoonful of ash which the police managed to recover for them."

News.title: Southport killer charged with prison attacks and possessing weapon
News.content:
Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has been charged with three attacks while in prison and possessing a weapon.

Police say the offences took place at HMP Belmarsh over six months from May to October 2025.

The 19-year-old murdered Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, Bebe King, six, and Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, and injured eight other children and two adults in an attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class in July 2024.

He was given a 52-year sentence in January 2025. Earlier this month he was moved to a secure psychiatric hospital.

Rudakubana is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court remotely on 11 September.

He has been charged with the following four offences:

Assault on an emergency worker on 6 May 2025

Attempted grievous bodily harm on 8 May 2025

Unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon in prison on 26 June 2025

Assault on an emergency worker on 28 October 2025

In May 2025, it was reported boiling water had been thrown on a prison officer at Belmarsh. They were taken to hospital and discharged on the same day.

When Rudakubana was jailed, the judge was unable to impose a whole life order due to him being under-18 when he carried out the attack. He will likely never be released.

On 23 July, the MoJ confirmed Rudakubana was transferred from HMP Belmarsh to Broadmoor, a high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.

Under the Mental Health Act, the MoJ is likely to have had no choice but to accept doctors' recommendations about whether Rudakubana could be held safely in prison.

The decision to transfer him was criticised by a lawyer representing the families of victims.

News.title: Puberty blockers trial can start recruiting children after judge rejects legal challenge
News.content:
A high-profile clinical trial of drugs that can delay puberty in children questioning their gender can go ahead after the High Court rejected a legal challenge by campaigners.

The Pathways trial, run by researchers at King's College London (KCL), will start recruiting more than 220 children aged between 11 and 16 years old from 1 August.

The study was commissioned to assess the benefits or risks of puberty blockers, after a landmark review into gender services found the evidence for treating young people with the drugs was "remarkably weak".

Campaigners who brought the legal action had argued the safeguards in place were inadequate and raised concerns about the long-term physical and psychological effects on young people.

The judge, Mr Justice Chamberlain, refused the application for a judicial review saying that none of the claims made by the campaigners had a realistic chance of success.

He said that each patient involved in the trial will have been assessed over "many months" by specialist doctors who will have "formed the opinion that a child has a reasonable prospect of receiving a clinical benefit from the treatment".

A spokeswoman for KCL welcomed the court's decision, saying the "safety and welfare of young people will remain our highest priority in carrying out this research".

Campaigners, including parents of gender-questioning children, said they were disappointed by the decision saying the "world is watching" a case which has "global implications and high stakes".

News.title: Andy Burnham to give regional mayors share of income tax
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will give all mayors of city regions in England a share of income tax revenue for the first time, as part of his drive to transfer power from Westminster to local leaders.

Burnham will also allow English strategic authorities to keep some cash from business rates collected in their areas, and gain greater control over services such as housing, transport, skills.

The government has not yet decided the exact portion of taxes mayors will get, with more details to be announced when Chancellor John Healey delivers his first budget in the autumn.

Opposition parties said the plans lacked detail and could lead to areas with weaker economies losing out on funding.

But Burnham said the move would "make good" on his pledge to "bring power home" to "every postcode in the country".

"Under our plans, more of the taxes raised in a community will stay in that community," the prime minister added.

First Secretary of State Louise Haigh told BBC Radio 4's Today programme areas without mayors would also benefit from investment because devolution powers would be held by new strategic authorities across England.

Strategic authorities bring together local councils to control regional issues such as transport and economic development, with decisions taken collectively by council leaders rather than a single elected mayor.

But Labour backbencher Perran Moon said the government's plans were "discriminatory" and could create a "two-tier system".

The MP for Camborne and Redruth in Cornwall said the area would never have a mayor or become a combined authority and so risked not having access to devolved powers that other areas would have.

"What we're asking government to do is to provide us with the same powers, the same funding that mayoral combined authorities have without the requirement of becoming a combined authority or having a mayor."

The government has also announced that mayors will be given a fast-track route to building new tramways, roads and light rail in their areas.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the threshold at which local leaders need to seek approval for projects will rise to Â£500m, up from Â£200m.

News.title: England and Wales on course for driest July on record
News.content:
England and Wales are on course for their driest July since records began 190 years ago.

The Met Office reports that England has seen just 5.6mm of rainfall up to 30 July â just 8% of its long-term meteorological average for the month and less than half of the previous record of 13.4mm set in 1911.

For Wales it is 7.9mm of rainfall, also 8% of its long-term average for the month and almost a third of the previous record of 22.6mm, again set in 1911.

The UK as a whole is currently on track for its third driest July, and driest nationally since 1868.

News.title: Budget to be held in October, Healey announces
News.content:
Chancellor John Healey has announced the date of his first Budget will be Wednesday, 28 October.

In aâ¯video message,â¯ he said: "This will be a Budget that moves money and power out of Westminster, and into every postcode around Britain.

"It will be built on fiscal discipline. It will meet our fiscal rules. It'll give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future. Now, let's get on with the job."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government will stick to Labour's fiscal rules on spending and borrowing as well as the party's 2024 manifesto pledges not to increase income tax, VAT or national insurance contributions.

Burnham also said he will honour the fiscal rules imposed by Healey's predecessor Rachel Reeves, which include a pledge to balance day-to-day spending with tax revenues by the end of the decade.

An influential think tank said earlier this week that the prime minister only has a small margin of error to do this, and that Healey may have to cut spending or raise taxes to meet Burnham's policy priorities such as such as extra defence spending and better social care.

Healey was Defence Secretary under Keir Starmer, but resigned after a row over defence spending commitments - saying he was "certain" that Britain shouldl lift its spending to 3% by 2030.

But questioned about funding on Thursday, Burnham's Defence Secretary Wes Streeting repeatedly refused to commit to that target.

"Before we set out specific spending commitments, we will also set out how we pay for them at the same time," he said.

News.title: Sainsbury's agrees to sell Argos for £120m
News.content:
Sainsbury's has agreed to sell Argos for Â£120m after a long process of trying to offload it as the supermarket chain aims to focus on its main food business.

Sainsbury's said it would be "business as usual" for Argos customers, staff, and suppliers. Shoppers will see no change as Argos will still operate in Sainsbury's shops, sell Habitat products, and offer Nectar points.

The buyer, Swift Partners, is a company that has been created to buy the brand and includes former Co-operative Group boss Richard Pennycook.

There are 667 Argos shops across the UK, with 201 operating as standalone stores and 466 operating within Sainsbury's. It also has more than 450 collection points.

Founded in 1973, Argos opened shops where customers browsed its catalogues and placed their orders, with products being delivered to tills from warehouses connected to the stores.

The Argos catalogue, once described by comedian Bill Bailey as the "laminated book of dreams", used to be a physical book.

Argos no longer prints this hefty tome, with its full range now available online instead. In store, customers can browse the product collection on tablet computers.

Sainsbury's has been trying to sell Argos - which has been seen as an underperforming brand - for some time.

Sainsbury's bought Argos â together with Habitat and all the other retail brands owned by Home Retail Group â in 2016 for Â£1.4bn. It then sold Argos financial services, which runs the Argos card, for around Â£720m in 2024.

In September last year, its talks to sell the rest of Argos to Chinese online retailer JD.com fell through.

Sainsbury's chief executive Simon Roberts said that all of Argos's nearly 14,000 staff would be transferred over to Swift Partners as part of the deal.

He also confirmed that Argos would continue to operate in Sainsbury's shops; Nectar will continue to be used across both Argos and Sainsbury's; and Sainsbury's will continue to sell Habitat products

Swift Partners' Pennycook said he believed "strongly in Argos's future and see real opportunities to invest and build on its progress".

The deal is expected to be completed in February next year.

Pennycook said there was the potential to open new standalone Argos shops â and did not rule out the possibility of the return of its print catalogue.

News.title: Passenger on British Airways mayday flight describes fear and shout of 'I don't want to die'
News.content:
A passenger on a British Airways flight that issued a distress call on approach to Heathrow Airport earlier this month has described the rising fear in the cabin and a lack of information from the crew.

Edward Killiwick had been travelling back from a friend's birthday party with his partner Julie, on the flight from Dusseldorf in Germany on 6 July.

He said passengers were told that the landing had been aborted, and then he felt a "very violent manoeuvre" and "did think we could crash". He and his partner had to comfort a woman who "completely lost it and started screaming, 'I don't want to die'".

The flight landed safely, but the incident is being investigated with assistance from BA.

The UK's Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) said it was "investigating a serious incident", and France's accident investigation authority, the BEA, said on Wednesday that the plane, an Airbus A320, had issued a distress call.

Edward said: "The violent manoeuvre almost felt like it was avoiding another aircraft. You could feel the engines going at full power.

"It was a bit odd going around in a holding pattern with no information. I thought if they're not talking, then they're not in a good place."

He said they were in a holding pattern for about 15 minutes.

The BEA said that as the plane approached Heathrow, there was a data system failure which triggered a stall warning.

The crew then flew the aircraft in a different mode called "alternate law", which removes some automated flight protection systems. Another stall warning then occurred at 3,000 feet â which experts say was likely to have been just miles away from the airport.

The urgency call the crew had already made was upgraded to mayday, indicating imminent danger.

A British Airways spokesperson said the airline was assisting the AAIB with its investigation and was not legally able to comment further at this stage.

Edward said: "I was definitely scared. After the violent manoeuvre I thought, there is definitely something very badly wrong here. I did think we could crash.

"I did think it was a possibility, and I think everyone else did."
